newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to open Taiwan dollar options by year-end.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to open Taiwan dollar options by year-end.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank said on Friday it plans to open trading in local dollar options by the end of 1996 in a bid to expand the domestic foreign exchange market.

"The central bank just held a meeting with the Ministry of Finance, and both sides in principle decided to open the Taiwan dollar options trading by the end of this year," a central bank official told reporters.
The move aims to offer Taiwan firms more risk-avoiding tools and help expand the country's foreign exchange market, he said.
The official said the move will offer trading options for Taiwan companies and investors in exchanges between Taiwan dollar and other foreign currencies.
The central bank has already allowed foreign exchange options trading between foreign currencies.

The central bank is also considering allowing foreign exchange futures trading related to the Taiwan dollar after the domestic futures market, scheduled to start in the second half of 1997, is formally established, the official said.

Taiwan, which started financial derivatives trading in early 1994, so far allows more than 10 derivatives to be traded, including cross-currency swaps, margin, option and interest rate swap trading, the central bank said.
